specialization: Electrical and telecommunications engineer. This is my personal site.
degree: BEng Electrical and Telecommunications Engineering, Moi University, Second Class Honours (2020-2025)

about.label: About
about.title: Engineer by training. Builder by practice.
about.body: I am Gerard, an electrical and telecommunications engineer. VersaCarte is my personal practice and the name I ship under. It is not a company that makes the work for me. I design, build and document the projects you see here.
about.mission: I work across power, telecoms, firmware and full-stack software so a system can be understood from the sensor or circuit through to the interface people use.
values: I own the work from schematic, firmware or API through to the product people touch
I document architecture so others can audit, extend and hand it on
I design for real conditions: variable power, connectivity, devices and payments

hero.title: I keep my engineering work here
hero.subtitle: I trained in electrical and telecommunications engineering. VersaCarte is my personal site. Resphinx, FileSendNX and the traffic monitor are the projects on it.

vision.label: About
vision.title: Engineer by training. Builder by practice.
vision.body: I am Gerard. The projects on this site are work I created, including Resphinx, FileSendNX, Smart Traffic Control and related systems. They are not studio output from a company team.
vision.imageAlt: Hands writing code on a laptop

items.title: Electrical & telecoms
items.body: Most of my training is power and telecoms. Attachment work was at Kenya Power and in public-works design.

items.title: Software when a project needs it
items.body: I write a screen or a phone app when the engineering needs one. It sits next to the rest of the work.

items.title: Hardware that reports back
items.body: The traffic project is sensors at a junction, a radio link and a dashboard on the other end.

why.label: How I work
why.title: One person from schematic to shipped interface
why.body: You work with me directly. Hardware, firmware, APIs and mobile or web UI stay in one thread instead of three vendors handing off blame.
